description: We are a team interested in data science, AI, and Earth observation. We’re looking for a teammate with knowledge of geographical data, GIS, environmental science, and Earth systems to help us interpret NASA datasets and understand environmental changes. If you’re interested in climate, geography, mapping, or environmental analysis, we’d love to have you!
summary:
ImpactLens is a web app that lets anyone check whether our planet is really changing, and how fast. It follows one chain of cause and effect: ice melts in Greenland, Antarctica and the Himalayas, global sea level rises, and coastal Bangladesh loses land and faces shifting monsoon rains.

On an interactive 3D globe, users pick a variable, a region and a time range. The app runs proper trend statistics (Mann-Kendall test, Sen's slope with a 95% interval) and explains the result in plain language: is the change real, and how fast is it? An AI assistant can set up analyses from a simple question and summarise the results, but every number comes from the app's own statistics, never from the AI. The data comes from NASA and partner records, including GRACE/GRACE-FO, MERRA-2, GPM IMERG and NASA-SSH.

This matters because climate trends are often misread. ImpactLens turns NASA's Earth observations into clear, honest answers that people can trust.

Next:
-Add variables such as urban growth and vegetation.
-Expand coverage to more coastal countries.
details:
What it does

ImpactLens helps anyone answer a simple but often misread question: is this part of the Earth system really changing, and how fast? It follows one chain of cause and effect:

  • Ice loss in Greenland, Antarctica and the Himalayas
  • Global and regional sea-level rise
  • Impact on coastal Bangladesh: submerged land and changing monsoon rainfall

How it works

Users explore an interactive 3D globe with polar views and animated NASA map layers, such as monthly ice and water mass change from GRACE and air temperature anomalies from MERRA-2.

They pick a variable, a region (from ice sheets down to all 64 districts of Bangladesh) and a time range, then press Run analysis.

A statistics engine in the browser computes:

  • Mann-Kendall trend test, corrected for autocorrelation
  • Sen's slope with a 95% interval
  • How many years of data are needed to detect a trend
  • Bootstrap comparisons between regions or variables

User Can Download the Charts And reports

The engine is checked against reference Python implementations.

Results appear as:

  • A plain-language verdict and the key numbers
  • Interactive charts: time series, anomaly, annual change, sea-level equivalent
  • A "Data source and honesty" block listing the dataset, version, DOI and any gaps
An AI assistant can set up and run an analysis from a simple question, such as "Are the Himalayan glaciers losing ice?", and summarise the result. It can only use the app's own tools, so every number it quotes comes from the engine, never from the AI.

Users can also:

  • Download a report
  • Export charts
  • Check their own data files against the app's format

Benefits and intended impact

  • Students, teachers, journalists and local decision-makers get statistically sound answers without needing statistics training.
  • It links distant ice loss to its effects on a vulnerable delta, so global change becomes personal.
  • It pushes back on two common mistakes: calling a noisy year a trend, and dismissing a real trend as noise.

Data

NASA and partner records:

  • GRACE/GRACE-FO
  • MERRA-2
  • GPM IMERG
  • NASA-SSH
  • JPL sea-level reconstruction
  • ITS_LIVE
  • IMBIE
  • Landsat-based JRC Global Surface Water

Anyone can click the 'i' icon to see details about all the data sources

Tools and technologies

  • Web app: TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS
  • Globe: CesiumJS with the NASA GIBS Blue Marble base map
  • Charts: ECharts
  • Statistics: our own engine running in Web Workers
  • Data pipeline: Python (xarray, NumPy), turning the datasets into compact JSON and image files
  • AI: open-weight LLM (gpt-oss) through Groq, with tool calling
  • Hosting: Netlify, deployed from GitHub
  • No hardware was needed

What makes it creative

  • It tells a story rather than showing a dashboard: ice to sea to land.
  • Its AI operates the app instead of inventing answers.
  • It is honest about uncertainty: results with too little data say "cannot tell yet", and the app shows how many more years are needed.
  • On the ice-change map, brighter and redder means more ice lost.

Factors we considered

  • Scientific honesty: we account for autocorrelation and short records, never fill gaps, never claim a cause from a correlation, and always show the 95% interval.
  • Clarity: plain language and "Describe" pop-ups for each variable.
  • Data validation: we cross-checked independent sources; for example, GRACE and IMBIE agree for Greenland (-249 vs -253 Gt/yr).
  • Access: free hosting, small static data files, a phone layout, keyboard navigation, reduced motion and readable contrast.
  • Privacy: user files are checked in the browser and never uploaded.
